scope: All 276 mapped Échezeaux parcels inventoried; all 36 recorded right-holder groups triaged. Not an exhaustive search of every cadastral reference or inaccessible archive.
rules: Candidate names are research hypotheses, never verified farmers.
Rights as of 2025-01-01, modern cadastral geometry and estate descriptions are different evidence.
A reviewed-at date or webpage crawl date is not a farming date.
Unmatched rights do not mean no owner or no farmer.
A cru intersection does not establish that the whole cadastral parcel is planted or farmed.
No automatic assignment from area, adjacency, named area, wine bottler, manager or similar company name.

sources.title: DVF+ open-data (Cerema), sale and exchange deeds, Flagey-Échezeaux, 2014–2025
sources.finding: The hash-pinned April 2026 regional release keeps every deed since January 2014 (data.gouv.fr keeps five years), without party names. 26 deeds touch 45 Échezeaux parcels. Company purchases are followed by the buyer's first record in the next January rights file, sometimes a year later. Prices and addresses are not kept.

sources.title: Winehog: Terroir View – Jean-Marc Millot Echezeaux "Cuvée 1949"

Millot owns 0.5981 ha of Échezeaux du Dessus, plots 798, 799 and 800, from the Gouroux family of his wife; a 1986 court case against Mongeard-Mugneret gave Millot the right to vinify them. Cuvée 1949 (from 2017) comes from part of 798/799.

sources.title: Winehog: Terroir View – Berthaut-Gerbet Echezeaux
sources.finding: Premium article supplied by the repository owner; only facts are recorded. From the 2018 vintage 0.2126 ha: Les Quartiers de Nuits 360 (0.0975 ha), part of Les Treux 508 (0.0276 ha; the rest presumably rented by another domaine) and Champs Traversins 821, 822 (0.0875 ha, from 2018). Amélie Berthaut took over two thirds of the Domaine Gerbet vineyards; first Échezeaux vintage 2013.

sources.title: Winehog: Terroir Insight – Domaine Jean Grivot Echezeaux
sources.finding: Premium article supplied by the repository owner; only facts are recorded. Grivot Échezeaux from seven plots, 0.8460 ha: Les Cruots ou Vignes Blanches 172, 176, 792, 794, 599 (0.7970 ha) and Champs Traversins 590, 593 (0.0490 ha). 172/176 presumably via the Jayer family; 792/794 and presumably 590/593 from the Lamadon holdings divided in 2006 between Liger-Belair (métayage), the Lamarche family and the Grivot family.

holders.finding: The estate's Échezeaux area is consistent with this holder group. Identity, acreage and appellation together support a candidate; no current parcel-by-parcel operation statement was found.
The GFA is a landholder. The estate produces Échezeaux, but no reviewed lease establishes the operator of each GFA parcel.
The estate names two vineyard areas and documents a 2017 métayage change. Its two cadastral parcels still require exact-reference and current-season confirmation.
Official registry corroborates the exact legal entity. Website retrieval failed; no current farming claim covers D0168, D0169 and D0519.

candidateNames: Domaine du Clos Frantin / Albert Bichot
holders.finding: The producer describes an approximately 1 ha Champs Traversins plot. D0760 is a candidate via Bichot recorded rights; acreage alone is not a cadastral join.
Estate description of 0.94 ha in Combe d'Orveaux corroborates vineyard context, not the exact current operation of D0340/D0352.
Faiveley's own legal notice explicitly gives SIREN 775567928 (CVVB). Its En Orveaux wine sheet supplies vineyard context. Exact current operation of the three recorded parcels remains unconfirmed.
The estate describes 0.76 ha Les Loachausses. D0183/D0709 are rights-based candidates, distinct from D0177/D0178 in the 2022 application.
The GFA is a landholding entity. Dujac's 0.6872 ha sheet supports an estate-level candidate; no exact lease or operation statement for D0306 reviewed.
The estate describes 0.53 ha Échezeaux du Dessus. Its precise scope, mapped area difference and current season remain to be checked.

ORVEAUX GFA (SIREN 984543470) is registered at Domaine Joseph Drouhin's office and managed by the Drouhin family; registered February 2024, parcels first recorded January 2025. The family publishes 0.41 ha of Échezeaux against 0.53 ha here, so not all may be farmed by the domaine.

A report hosted by Duband describes Feuillet entrusting vineyards to him; Duband also lists Échezeaux. The relationship is a useful operator lead but neither source names the four cadastral references. Winehog (2019) lists D0677 among Arnoux-Lachaux's Échezeaux plots, which conflicts with a Duband lead for that parcel.
Estate website lists Échezeaux. Current legal operating entity and parcel-specific farming remain to be established.
BND-labelled right-holder record does not name a farmer. No operator or documented predecessor/successor chain for these five modern references was located.
Secondary producer source connects Jack Confuron with Confuron-Cotetidot and Échezeaux. Requires primary legal-entity and exact-parcel farming confirmation.

Registry name GRPT FONCIER VIT GRD CRUS INVESTISSEMENT (SIREN 413823873) matches; its office is the Méo-Camuzet family's address in Vosne. Méo-Camuzet publishes 0.44 ha in Les Rouges du Bas; these three parcels there cover 0.45 ha. No lease or current operation reviewed.

Estate cuvée list and historical auction catalogue support the Bissey Échezeaux holding. An auction buyer or élevage house must not replace the farming domaine; D0510 still needs exact dated confirmation.

Official name search found GFA Héritiers Coudray, SIREN 477938294, now registered in Hérault and managed by the family. No link to a Burgundy domaine or tenant was found; the U-prefixed crosswalk remains unverified.

LES CRUOTS GFA (SIREN 930915806) is registered at the Rouget family's operating address in Flagey and managed by the family. Registered July 2024; these parcels first appear in the January 2025 file. It is a land company: no lease or current operation of these four parcels was reviewed.
The producer's 2023 sheet describes Champs Traversins and harvest. No cadastral reference identifies D0773 or confirms the current season.

Current estate history and secondary succession account suggest Jean-Charles Rion following Daniel Rion. Need transfer/lease covering D0665/D0666/D0667; do not copy the old holder name into current farmer.

GFA holds Les Treux. An auction lists a 2019 Bouchy bottle with Tardy bottling; this is not evidence Tardy farmed these five parcels, then or now. In December 2025 SCEA Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair applied to farm all five parcels; the application was suspended in April 2026.
Jadot importer describes Échezeaux holdings. Corporate/holding history is a lead, with no accepted cadastral operation crosswalk for D0638/D0771.

HOR Vignobles is owned by a foreign holding company, not a named domaine. Its accounts describe owned Échezeaux assets, and an indexed filing concerns SCI Les Climats. No farmer inferred from ownership or acreage.
Claire Naudin's management of the GFA and the estate's Les Rouges du Bas sheet support a lead. No parcel-specific lease reviewed; 2019 sheet and 2022 harvest do not establish 2026 farming.
Estate sheet describes Échezeaux production; exact cadastral holdings and current season unconfirmed.

GFA FAMILLE FOREY BJ (SIREN 937826790) shares its office and a manager with SCE du Domaine Forey Père & Fils. Registered November 2024; these parcels first appear in January 2025. The importer names Forey vines in Clos Saint-Denis and Les Treux, as here. No lease reviewed.
Estate lists Échezeaux; GFA holding is not an operating relationship. The broader estate holding must not be reconstructed by filling nearby unknown parcels.

Traversins has Christophe Roumier as president; a 2023 estate-visit report describes additional Champs Traversins vines. Neither identifies these five cadastral parcels or a 2026 operating lease. Reviewed company filing text did not establish a Flagey lease or parcel operation.

Estate history explicitly says only PART of the Gerbet vines joined Berthaut-Gerbet. Which of D0360/D0508/D0821, if any, is farmed by this domaine needs confirmation. Winehog (2019) names D0360, D0821 and part of D0508 as Berthaut-Gerbet plots; the remainder of D0508 is presumably farmed by another domaine.
Estate sheet describes farming 1.09 ha En Orveaux, versus approximately 0.22 ha in this rights group. That mismatch flags incomplete coverage; no additional parcels assigned by area or proximity.
Same-name operating estate is a candidate, but not proof of current farming of these two references. Kept separate from the GFA.
Legal notice records continuity from EARL Denis Thomas after a 2023 rename. Current farmer of D0203 remains unconfirmed.

ORIGINE, now LC, shares its Paris office with Domaine de la Pousse d'Or, and one person became manager of both in 2022. Pousse d'Or describes a quarter-acre in the Poulaillères held by its owner's holding company; D0313 is a 0.11 ha parcel there. No lease reviewed.

Bouchon Pourpre's link to Comte Liger-Belair is corporate. No accepted lease or exact-parcel current-operation evidence for D0673. SCEA Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair applied to farm D0673 in December 2025; instruction was suspended in April 2026, so no authorisation existed at that date.

SCI Les Climats, Beaune, is managed by a member of the Follin-Arbelet family; the name alone is not linked to a domaine. An indexed 2021 filing describes an En Orveaux asset transfer involving it. Ownership transfer is not farming evidence.

exactParcelEvents.summary: Dossier 2022-204, complete at 21/10/2022, 1.5050 ha across Vosne-Romanée and Flagey-Échezeaux; the receipt does not authorise cultivation. Geometry of D0177/D0178 is unchanged since January 2022. Printed D01776 is unresolved.
exactParcelEvents.appNote: Receipt of a complete application. It is not an authorisation, and the outcome was not published in the bulletins searched.

exactParcelEvents.applicant: SAS Domaine RC Les Grandes Vignes (Quincey)
exactParcelEvents.summary: Application filed 11/01/2022, complete 01/03/2022, CDOA opinion 25/05/2022; the same decision refuses Vosne-Romanée AB references to this applicant. Article 2 lists four communes without assigning each row; the section D rows are taken as Flagey-Échezeaux because the cédant holds these references there. D0665 is printed at 0.1157 ha, its cadastral area; D0666 at 0.0799 ha against 0.1157 ha, so its scope is unresolved. D0667, held by the same right holder, is not in the decision. Whether the applicant is connected to Domaine Jean-Charles Rion is not established.
exactParcelEvents.appNote: The same decision refuses the applicant other Vosne-Romanée parcels. Its list of communes is not split by parcel, so the commune is inferred from the previous operator. D0666 is printed at 0.0799 ha against a 0.1157 ha parcel, so its scope is unclear.

exactParcelEvents.summary: Dossier 2022-053, filed 07/03/2022, complete 28/03/2022; 0.7903 ha across Vosne-Romanée and Flagey-Échezeaux, all three Flagey references in Les Loächausses. The receipt is not an authorisation. D0774 was divided after January 2024.
exactParcelEvents.appNote: Receipt of a complete application. It is not an authorisation, and no decision was found in the bulletins searched.

exactParcelEvents.summary: Dossier 2022-113, filed 23/05/2022, with Vougeot A523/A524; 1.0719 ha in total. Both Flagey references are in Les Loächausses. The receipt states it does not authorise cultivation. D0775 was divided after January 2024.
exactParcelEvents.appNote: Receipt of a complete application. It states it does not authorise cultivation, and no decision was found in the bulletins searched.

exactParcelEvents.outcome: instruction suspended for eight months from 29 April 2026
exactParcelEvents.summary: The application covers 4.3080 ha in Flagey-Échezeaux, Boncourt-le-Bois, Vosne-Romanée and Vougeot belonging to SAS Bouchon Pourpre, GFA Domaine Bouchy et Amis, SCEA Nathalie Pacareau Lamarche and Mme Geneviève Lamarche; it also names Grands-Échezeaux D615 and D616. The region found the enlargement excessive and suspended the instruction, during which anyone may apply for the same land. As of the order, the applicant was not authorised to farm these parcels.
exactParcelEvents.appNote: Examination suspended for eight months from 29 April 2026 as an excessive enlargement. Anyone may apply for the same land meanwhile. Not an authorisation.

accessGaps: CVI records require cooperation from authorised holders; no private records accessed.
Public CartoBio polygons omit operator identity.
HOR Vignobles and Coudray PDF full text/render unavailable; indexed excerpts retained only as leads.

Regional bulletins 2019–2026 were read for Côte-d'Or DDT notices (2026 to the end of September). Farm-structure notices appear there regularly only from 2021; the Côte-d'Or departmental bulletins for 2016–2020 were later searched in full (31,966 pages, PR #412). Their only Flagey-Échezeaux vineyard decision (Maison Louis Bouillot, signed 18 November 2015, RAA 10 of 2016) prints section A references (A 9–11, 13, 15, 30–32, 893–900), none of them in the 276 mapped section D parcels, so it creates no parcel link. Departmental bulletins before 2016 and the five unresolved 2018 references remain unsearched, so "no decision found" means none in the searched corpus. The DDT notice page and cote-dor.gouv.fr refused automated access.
Cadastral lineage covers the 2019–2026 vintages only; earlier divisions are not traced.

DVF+ sale records start in January 2014 and end in November 2025, and name no party. Gifts, inheritances and transfers without a price are not in them. Deeds printed with a parcel reference retired before 2019 are not traced to today's parcels.

The Côte-d'Or prefecture site and pre-2016 departmental bulletins remain unsearched: cote-dor.gouv.fr rate-limits automated requests. SAFER legal notices were reached at annonces-legales.saferbfc.com (29 September 2026), but the site keeps only notices still open, so past SAFER sales remain unseen.
Winehog Premium articles were read only where supplied by the repository owner (Grivot, Arnoux-Lachaux, Millot, Berthaut-Gerbet); the Grands-Échezeaux articles and others only as public previews.

Producer holdings were collected from estate, importer, merchant and guide pages on 29 September 2026. Several merchant pages refused automated reading (403/429); figures seen only in search summaries were not recorded.

Court decisions were searched on Juricaf (29 September 2026). The Cour de cassation Judilibre search returned ten results for Flagey-Echezeaux once, then required a CAPTCHA; it was not bypassed, and the Judilibre API needs a registered key. Rulings are pseudonymised and were not re-identified. A second attempt on 29 September 2026 met a JavaScript and cookie check, which was not bypassed.

Gallica text pages now require a proof-of-work check that was not bypassed; the 1892 and c. 1920 guides were read from Internet Archive scans (OCR, names checked by eye). Lavalle (1855) was not found in a readable copy.

Company identities were checked on 29 September 2026 in BODACC notices and the official company search. U-prefixed DGFiP holders carry no SIREN, so each match rests on name, registered office, management family and first-recorded date together. Directors are summarised by family, not named. A land company is not a farmer.

historyFindings.title: Nicole Lamarche entity was named after Domaine François Lamarche
historyFindings.finding: SIREN 397738634 is recorded as FONCIER VITI DOM FRANCOIS LAMARCHE on 1 January 2020 and 2021 and as NICOLE LAMARCHE from 2022. The unchanged SIREN proves one renamed legal entity, which strengthens the identity link to the Lamarche domaine. There was no company record in 2019. Farming of the three parcels remains unconfirmed.

historyFindings.title: Anne Gros company rights begin in 2021
historyFindings.finding: ANNE GROS (SIREN 348024928) first appears on 1 January 2021; both references existed in 2019 without a company record. This dates recorded rights, not an operating start.

historyFindings.title: 2022 application references match today's geometry
historyFindings.finding: Geometry and recorded area of D0177 and D0178 (and Grands-Échezeaux D0093) are identical in the 1 January 2022 vintage and today, so the printed references in the November 2022 receipt denote today's parcels. Neither Échezeaux reference has a company record in any year 2019–2025, consistent with private ownership. The application's outcome and actual operation remain unconfirmed; D01776 appears in no vintage.

historyFindings.title: D0673 left Mongeard-Mugneret during 2024
historyFindings.finding: Both references were held by ASSURANCES DU CREDIT MUTUEL VIE until 2020 and by DOMAINE MONGEARD MUGNERET (SIREN 303514681) from 2021. On 1 January 2025 D0673 is held by BOUCHON POURPRE (SIREN 880909346). A Mongeard lead for D0673 rests on rights that ended during 2024.

historyFindings.title: Capitain parcels moved to Capitain-Gagnerot in 2020
historyFindings.finding: GFA DOMAINE FRANCOIS CAPITAIN ET FILS (SIREN 339012320) through 2020, SARL CAPITAIN GAGNEROT (SIREN 515620466) from 2021. A different SIREN means a transfer between entities. Family-name continuity supports the existing lead without proving farming.

historyFindings.title: Clerget parcel moved into the domaine company in 2023
historyFindings.finding: GFV CHRISTIAN ET ISABELLE CLERGET (SIREN 430384354) through 2023, SCEV DU DOMAINE CHRISTIAN CLERGET (SIREN 431340140) from 2024. Ownership by the domaine company is closer to the operator, but it is not a lease or operation record.

historyFindings.title: HOR Vignobles transfer to SCI Les Climats dated to 2022
historyFindings.finding: D0815 passes from HOR VIGNOBLES to SCI LES CLIMATS between the 2022 and 2023 files, while D0813 and D0814 stay with HOR. This places the En Orveaux transfer suggested by the indexed HOR filing on D0815. The farmer remains unresolved.

historyFindings.title: Traversins rights start on 1 January 2024
historyFindings.finding: No company record through 2023; TRAVERSINS (SIREN 911887461) from 1 January 2024. The timing matches the 2023 report of additional Champs Traversins vines. That strengthens the lead's timing, not its parcel scope or farming.

historyFindings.title: U22079769 is an undivided-ownership placeholder for former D0143
historyFindings.finding: PROPRIETAIRES DU BND 267 D0143 held D0143 from 2019 to 2024. The 2025 cadastre divides D0143 into these five references and the same record follows. It denotes co-owners of undivided property, not a company to identify; ask the owners directly.

historyFindings.title: Family land companies first recorded in 2025
historyFindings.finding: GFA FAMILLE FOREY BJ, GROUPEMENT FONCIER VITICOLE DE ORVEAUX and LES CRUOTS first appear on 1 January 2025 on references that existed earlier without a company record. BODACC dates their registration to February, July and November 2024, consistent with family land moving into land-holding companies that year. Their U-numbers carry no SIREN, so the identity rests on name, date, registered office and managing family together; the companies are owners, not proven farmers.

historyFindings.title: Other first company records, 2023–2024
historyFindings.finding: DOMAINE ARNOUX - LACHAUX (D0161), EARL DOMAINE FAIVRE (D0203) and DOMAINE D'EUGENIE (D0340) first appear on 1 January 2024, ORIGINE (D0313) on 1 January 2023. These are recent acquisitions or transfers into a company; ask for the deed or lease date together with operation evidence.

historyFindings.title: Romanée-Conti record reformatted, parcels unchanged
historyFindings.finding: The same four references move from a MAJIC-only record (2019) through a provisional U-number (2020) to SIREN 778269407 (2021), as SC DOM DE LA ROMANEE CONTI becomes DOMAINE DE LA ROMANEE CONTI. This is consistent with reformatting rather than a sale, but the file alone cannot prove identity.

historyFindings.title: Split parcels with no company record in any year
historyFindings.finding: These references were created by dividing earlier parcels after 2019. Neither they nor their predecessors carry a company record in any year, which points to private owners. The legal-entity files cannot identify them; only owners, notaries or shared CVI extracts can.

historyFindings.title: Dujac land company sharecropped its vines to the operating company, 1997–2015
historyFindings.finding: A 2009 tax ruling records a métayage lease from SCE du Domaine Dujac to Société Domaine Dujac SA covering vines in Flagey-Échezeaux, 1 July 1997 to 11 November 2015. It names no parcel, and today's recorded holder of D0306 is GFA du Domaine Dujac, whose identity with the SCE is not established. It shows that owning and farming entities of one domaine can differ; it does not show who farms D0306 now.

externalResearch.title: Hospices de Beaune, Cuvée Jean-Luc Bissey
externalResearch.finding: Winehog reproduces the cadastre entry "000 D 510, 4 380 m², Les Echezeaux du Dessus" and reports the 2011 donation to the Hospices by Jean-Luc Bissey, with Mongeard-Mugneret producing from it until 2011. Consistent with the 2019–2025 rights (HOSPICES CIVILS DE BEAUNE). Who cultivates for the Hospices is not stated.
externalResearch.appNote: Named by cadastral number: the Hospices de Beaune cuvée Jean-Luc Bissey, donated in 2011. Who cultivates it for the Hospices is not stated.

externalResearch.title: Jayer-Gilles plot, cadastre no 631
externalResearch.finding: Winehog names cadastre 631 as the Jayer-Gilles Échezeaux du Dessus plot, 0.5361 ha, in the Jayer family since 1933. Rights 2019–2025 record DOMAINE HOFFMANN-JAYER on D0631 (5 361 m²), consistent with the published area.
externalResearch.appNote: Named by cadastral number as the Jayer-Gilles plot, in the Jayer family since 1933.

externalResearch.title: Niquet-Jayer plot, cadastre no 632
externalResearch.finding: Winehog names cadastre 632 as Niquet-Jayer's 0.5285 ha, with no own bottling after 2003 and the wine "now produced by or sold to a négociant". D0632 has no company record in any year 2019–2025, consistent with private family ownership. The négociant or farmer is not named.
externalResearch.appNote: Named by cadastral number as the Niquet-Jayer plot. Its wine is now made by or sold to a négociant, who is not named.

externalResearch.title: Domaine des Perdrix, Échezeaux du Dessus
externalResearch.finding: Winehog 2014 area; the parcel set is reconstructed by this register because the published area equals their exact cadastral sum. Winehog lists 0.8730 ha, marked not confirmed; D0620 and D0621 total 8 730 m² and carry no company record.
externalResearch.appNote: The published area (0.8730 ha) equals this parcel set exactly, but the article does not name the parcels. Marked "not confirmed" by the author.

externalResearch.title: Jean-Marc Millot: three named plots in Échezeaux du Dessus
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (January 2019) names cadastre 798, 799 and 800, 0.5981 ha, owned through the Gouroux family; the areas equal the cadastral sum exactly and confirm the earlier area reconstruction. None has a company record, consistent with private family ownership. A 1986 court case against Mongeard-Mugneret gave Millot the right to vinify these plots, so Mongeard had farmed them before. Cuvée 1949, from 2017, comes from part of D0798/D0799.
externalResearch.appNote: Three plots totalling 0.5981 ha, owned through the wife’s family. A 1986 court case against Mongeard-Mugneret gave Millot the right to vinify them.

externalResearch.title: Cécile Tremblay, Échezeaux du Dessus
externalResearch.finding: Winehog 2014 area; the parcel set is reconstructed by this register because the published area equals their exact cadastral sum. Winehog lists 0.1775 ha, not confirmed, from the Jayer family share sharecropped until 2002; D0189 and D0190 total 1 775 m² and carry no company record.
externalResearch.appNote: The published area (0.1775 ha) equals this parcel set exactly, but the article does not name the parcels. Marked "not confirmed" by the author.

externalResearch.title: Mongeard-Mugneret, Échezeaux du Dessus
externalResearch.finding: Winehog 2014 area; the parcel set is reconstructed by this register because the published area equals their exact cadastral sum. Winehog lists 0.3300 ha, not confirmed; D0668–D0670 total 3 300 m² and carry no company record.
externalResearch.appNote: The published area (0.3300 ha) equals this parcel set exactly, but the article does not name the parcels. Marked "not confirmed" by the author.

externalResearch.title: Michel Noëllat, Échezeaux du Dessus — conflicts with recorded rights
externalResearch.finding: Winehog 2014 area; the parcel set is reconstructed by this register because the published area equals their exact cadastral sum. Winehog lists 0.5097 ha, not confirmed; these five references total 5 097 m². The recorded rights conflict: D0191/D0192 are held by GFA Mongeard Mugneret from 2019, D0671–D0673 by Mongeard companies (D0671/D0673 after Crédit Mutuel until 2020) and D0673 by Bouchon Pourpre from 2025. Treat the 2014 attribution as unresolved.
externalResearch.appNote: The published area (0.5097 ha) equals this parcel set, but it conflicts with the recorded owners, so it is left unresolved.

externalResearch.title: Liger-Belair added an Échezeaux du Dessus plot from 2020
externalResearch.finding: Winehog reports a new Échezeaux du Dessus plot from the 2020 vintage without its location. D0673, in Échezeaux du Dessus, passed from Mongeard to Bouchon Pourpre (a company connected with Comte Liger-Belair) during 2024. The dates are compatible but do not identify the plot.
externalResearch.appNote: Liger-Belair added an Échezeaux du Dessus plot from 2020, location not given. The dates fit, but it does not identify this parcel.

externalResearch.title: Liger-Belair Échezeaux holdings before 2020
externalResearch.finding: Six plots totalling 0.6157 ha: two in Les Cruots ou Vignes Blanches (0.3299 ha), Champs Traversins and Clos Saint-Denis. No cadastral references; a research target for those climats.

externalResearch.title: Les Loächausses: former Gros Frère et Sœur monopole
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (2011) describes Les Loächausses as formerly a Gros Frère et Sœur monopole and lists Gros Frère et Sœur and Anne Gros there. The 2022 applications by Michel Gros and AF Gros cover D0181, D0184, D0558, D0774 and D0775 in Les Loächausses, and ANNE GROS holds D0183/D0709 there from 2021, consistent with a division of that holding.

externalResearch.title: Berthaut-Gerbet: four named plots, one only in part
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (March 2019) names 360 in Les Quartiers de Nuits (0.0975 ha), part of 508 in Les Treux (0.0276 ha) and, from the 2018 vintage, 821 and 822 in Champs Traversins (0.0875 ha), 0.2126 ha in total. D0360 and D0821 + D0822 equal their cadastral areas exactly. D0508 is 901 m², so about 625 m² of a parcel held by the Gerbet Sirugue GFA is presumably farmed by another, unnamed domaine. D0360, D0508 and D0821 are held by GFA Domaine Gerbet Sirugue; D0822, divided with D0821 from former D0300 in 2019, has no company record. Amélie Berthaut took over two thirds of the Gerbet vineyards.
externalResearch.appNote: Four named plots (0.2126 ha) from the 2018 vintage. Only part of D0508 is Berthaut-Gerbet’s; the rest is presumably farmed by another domaine.

externalResearch.title: Domaine Jean Grivot: seven named Échezeaux plots
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (May 2019) names cadastre 172, 176, 792, 794 and 599 in Les Cruots ou Vignes Blanches and 590, 593 in Champs Traversins as the source of the Grivot Échezeaux. Published areas equal the cadastral sums exactly (7 970 m² and 490 m²). D0792 and D0794 were divided during 2022; their evidence reaches D0826/D0827 and D0828/D0829 only through accepted lineage, and those rows are labelled as inherited. None of the plots has a company record in any year 2019–2025, consistent with private family ownership. The article describes farming for the Grivot Échezeaux as of 2019, not a dated current lease.
externalResearch.appNote: Seven named plots (0.8460 ha) in Les Cruots ou Vignes Blanches and Champs Traversins.

externalResearch.title: Lamadon holdings divided in 2006
externalResearch.finding: Winehog reports that the Lamadon family stopped production in 2006 and divided its plots between Louis-Michel Liger-Belair (métayage), the Lamarche family and the Grivot family; Grivot received 792/794 and presumably 590/593. The Liger-Belair and Lamarche shares are not identified by cadastral number.
externalResearch.appNote: The Lamadon holdings were divided in 2006 between Liger-Belair (métayage), the Lamarche family and Grivot.

externalResearch.title: Domaine Arnoux-Lachaux: four named plots in Les Rouges du Bas
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (May 2019) names cadastre 818, 819, 820 (formerly 206; 0.4535 ha) and 677 (0.1669 ha); the published areas equal the cadastral areas exactly. Rights agree for D0820 (DOMAINE ARNOUX - LACHAUX); D0818/D0819 have no company record. D0677 is recorded to FRANCOIS FEUILLET, so the article implies that Arnoux-Lachaux farmed a Feuillet-owned parcel in 2019. That conflicts with the holder-level Duband lead for D0677; both remain unconfirmed. Former reference 206 predates the 2019 cadastre vintage and is not traced. D0161, held by Arnoux-Lachaux from 2024, is not in the 2019 article.
externalResearch.appNote: Four named plots in Les Rouges du Bas. D0677 is recorded to another owner, and this conflicts with an earlier lead.

externalResearch.title: Gérard Mugneret, Les Quartiers de Nuits (métayage)
externalResearch.finding: Domaine Gérard Mugneret states that it sharecrops 0.6462 ha in Les Quartiers de Nuits owned by Domaine Georges Mugneret-Gibourg. That equals the cadastral area of D0362 (6 462 m²), the owner's only parcel in this lieu-dit. The page is undated and names no parcel.
externalResearch.appNote: The farming domaine states it sharecrops 0.6462 ha here for Mugneret-Gibourg: exactly this parcel's registered area, and the owner's only parcel in Les Quartiers de Nuits. Undated; parcel not named.

externalResearch.title: Fabrice Vigot métayage, Les Rouges du Bas, ended 2017
externalResearch.finding: Fabrice Vigot states 59.63 ares in Les Rouges du Bas "en métayage Mugneret-Gibourg"; Mugneret-Gibourg's only parcel there, D0195, measures 5 965 m² in the cadastre (5 963 m² mapped). Mugneret-Gibourg reports the first harvest of vines formerly sharecropped by Vigot in 2017, so Vigot's page predates that return.
externalResearch.producer: Domaine Georges Mugneret-Gibourg (since 2017; earlier Fabrice Vigot, métayage)
externalResearch.appNote: Fabrice Vigot sharecropped 59.63 ares here for Mugneret-Gibourg, matching this parcel's area. Mugneret-Gibourg reports taking these vines back for the 2017 harvest.

externalResearch.title: Clos Saint-Denis D 152 in a 2007 inheritance ruling
externalResearch.finding: The Dijon appeal court lists "section D no 152, Clos Saint Denis, 3 a 13 ca": exactly D0152's cadastral area (313 m²). In 2002–2007 it belonged to an undivided family estate and had been farmed since 25 December 1982 by one heir under a long-term rural lease. The ruling is pseudonymised; the family is not identified here. The later partition and today's farmer are unknown.
externalResearch.appNote: Named by parcel number in a 2007 court ruling: part of a family estate, farmed since 1982 by one heir under a long-term lease. The ruling is pseudonymised; who farms it today is unknown.

externalResearch.title: Liger-Belair, Les Cruots ou Vignes Blanches (area reconstruction)
externalResearch.finding: Liger-Belair publishes 0.3299 ha in Cruots ou Vignes Blanches, and Winehog describes two plots from the 2006 Lamadon division (métayage). D0793 (2 992 m²) and D0795 (307 m²) total exactly 3 299 m²; among parcels in this lieu-dit without a company record, the only other exact combination includes Grivot's named plots. The two parcels alternate with Grivot's former D0792 and D0794, also from the Lamadon division. This register reconstructs the set; the estate does not name the parcels.
externalResearch.appNote: Liger-Belair's published 0.3299 ha in Les Cruots equals D0793 + D0795 exactly. They alternate with Grivot's plots from the same 2006 Lamadon division. Reconstructed from areas; the estate names no parcel.

externalResearch.title: Liger-Belair, Clos Saint-Denis (area match, weak)
externalResearch.finding: Liger-Belair publishes 0.0312 ha in Clos Saint-Denis. D0155 (312 m², no company record) is the only exact match; D0152 (313 m²) differs by 1 m² and has its own court history. D0155 was sold on 13 October 2025 (DVF+). A single small parcel is a weak identification.
externalResearch.appNote: Liger-Belair's published 0.0312 ha in Clos Saint-Denis equals this parcel exactly, but a neighbouring 313 m² parcel is almost as close. Weak; the parcel was sold in October 2025.

externalResearch.title: Faiveley, En Orveaux (area equals its three company parcels)
externalResearch.finding: Faiveley states it owns 0 ha 83 a 35 ca in En Orveaux. The three parcels recorded to CVVB (SIREN 775567928, Faiveley's legal entity) total exactly 8 335 m² in the cadastre (440 + 4 941 + 2 954). The published holding is therefore these three parcels and nothing more; it adds nothing to the unrecorded En Orveaux land.
externalResearch.appNote: Faiveley states it owns 0 ha 83 a 35 ca in En Orveaux: exactly the cadastral total of its company's three parcels (D0331, D0335, D0653). Owner-stated; current operation is not separately confirmed.

producerHoldings.finding: Sharecrops land recorded to Mugneret-Gibourg (D0362).
